name: birt-rptdesign
description: Syntax highlighting and JavaScript linting for script blocks embedded in BIRT report design files.

commands.title: BIRT: Lint all report designs in workspace
BIRT: Open script block in a JavaScript editor
BIRT: Encode script characters the way BIRT Designer does

birtRptdesign.lint.enabled.description: Report JavaScript problems found in <method> and <expression> blocks.

birtRptdesign.lint.ecmaVersion.description: ECMAScript version used to parse embedded scripts. Keep this permissive and use the Rhino compatibility check to flag constructs your BIRT engine cannot run.

birtRptdesign.lint.rhinoCompatibility.description: Warn about modern JavaScript constructs that BIRT's Rhino script engine may not support.

birtRptdesign.lint.rhinoUnsupported.description: Which constructs the Rhino compatibility check reports. Tune this to the BIRT version you deploy to.

birtRptdesign.lint.undefinedGlobals.description: Warn when a script reads an identifier that is never declared or assigned anywhere in the same file and is not a known BIRT or JavaScript global. Useful for catching typos; may be noisy if scripts rely on globals set by other reports or libraries.

birtRptdesign.lint.extraGlobals.description: Additional global names to treat as defined by the undefined-globals check.

birtRptdesign.lint.delay.description: Milliseconds to wait after a change before re-linting.

enumDescriptions: Pool script libraries from the whole workspace, matching the single global scope BIRT's engine builds.
Only use script libraries under the closest ancestor directory. Catches more typos, but flags cross-region calls.
birtRptdesign.lint.globalScope.description: How the undefined-globals check resolves functions defined in shared script libraries.

birtRptdesign.lint.globalScriptDirs.description: Directories (relative to a workspace folder) holding .js and .rptlibrary files whose top-level declarations count as globals.

birtRptdesign.encodeEntitiesOnSave.markdownDescription: On save, escape `&` as `&` inside `<method>` and `<text-property>` CDATA, matching how BIRT Designer writes report files. `<`, `>` and `"` are left alone, because BIRT does not escape those inside CDATA.
